children: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy has secured orders worth more than Rs 9.85 billion across India and South Africa, covering a 534.3 MWp solar project and 616 MWh of battery storage

Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy (SWREL) has secured renewable energy orders worth more than Rs 9.85 billion, strengthening its solar engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) and battery energy storage system (BESS) portfolio as demand for utility-scale clean power and grid flexibility accelerates.

The company has won a 534.3 MWp solar project in Rajasthan from an independent power producer, while its international order covers two BESS projects with a combined storage capacity of 616 MWh in South Africa. The total order value includes taxes.

The Rajasthan contract covers the Balance of System package for the solar project and comes from a new customer. SWREL estimates that the project could help avoid around 0.80 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions after commissioning. The order comes as India continues to expand utility-scale renewable generation, increasing the need for EPC capabilities across solar infrastructure and systems required to integrate variable renewable power into the grid. Industry experts say the order mix reflects a broader shift in renewable energy investment, with developers increasingly looking beyond generation capacity towards infrastructure that can improve reliability, manage intermittency and support higher renewable penetration.

The South African contract includes two 308 MWh BESS projects and represents SWREL’s second-largest utility-scale BESS undertaking. The order was awarded by a Middle East-based renewable energy developer and is a repeat-customer engagement. Storage is also growing in importance in India, where rising renewable capacity is driving greater demand for flexible power assets. Battery storage is increasingly being positioned as a critical component for balancing electricity supply and demand as solar and wind generation expand. Experts note that the combination of large-scale solar and storage projects could become an increasingly important investment trend as power markets move towards higher shares of renewable electricity and require greater grid flexibility.
